rubrics.criterion: The route-resolution core of the mock transport no longer contains the parked strict engine's dispatch: the never-taken gated handover inside the live routing walk (the compile-time strictMatchingMode branch in MockTransport.findResponders), the strict walk it guards (MockTransport.findRespondersStrict), and both of its lookup strategies (exactStrictResponders, strictRegexpResponders) are removed from transport.go.
rubrics.rationale: This case's heart is a disabled routing engine hanging from one constant-gated branch in the live dispatcher of transport.go; a repair that leaves the branch, the walk, or either strategy in place does not resolve the parked-rollout removal even when the tree still compiles.

rubrics.criterion: The wiring that fed the strict walk is gone as well: the package-level method-value registry that listed its strategies (strictRouteFinders) and the transport-side hit-recording state handle (strictRouteStats) no longer exist in transport.go, rather than remaining emptied or referenced from live code.
rubrics.rationale: The registry deliberately mirrors the repository's own live findForKey registry idiom, so it reads as production wiring; keeping it (or the stats handle) preserves dead state that no shipped behavior consults and would leave the cleanup half-done.

rubrics.criterion: The rollout instrumentation cluster is fully removed from response.go: the mutex-guarded hit-collector type (routeStats), its constructor (newRouteStats), and both of its methods (record, snapshot) no longer appear in the package.
rubrics.rationale: The var-to-constructor-to-type-to-methods chain in response.go is the longest cross-file wiring of this instance, added solely to measure a rollout comparison that never ran; the transport-side handle covered by R2 is its only client.

rubrics.criterion: The strict matching policy drafted next to the live combinators is removed: matcherFuncAll (the nil-forbidding combination helper) and strictRequestBodyMatcher (the strict body-matching condition builder) are deleted from match.go, while the tolerant combinators the library ships (matcherFuncOr, matcherFuncAnd) and the shipped body-inspection helpers keep their behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The parked siblings were written as near-mirror twins of live matchers in match.go, so this item grades both halves of the trap at once: the parked twins gone, the shipped semantics intact.

rubrics.criterion: The superseded strict activation knob is removed from env.go (strictEnvVarName and strictModeEnabled, including every reference to the HTTPMOCK_STRICT variable), while httpmock.Disabled keeps reading exactly the GONOMOCKS variable with unchanged semantics.
rubrics.rationale: env.go models the abandoned first phase of the rollout: an environment knob drafted beside the real one and never consulted. Removing the parked knob must not disturb the single live activation switch sitting beside it.

rubrics.criterion: The internal canonical route-key cluster is removed from internal/route_key.go: the routeKeyV2 wrapper type, its normalizing method strictKey, and the canonicalRouteKey converter - together with any import left used only by that cluster (the strings import) - while the exported RouteKey (registration keying, NO_RESPONDER sentinel, String rendering) is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The rollout crosses the package boundary into the internal key representation, so the repair must follow it there; leaving the v2 key or an orphan import behind leaves both a remnant and a build break.

rubrics.criterion: Shipped route resolution is left intact: the tolerant fallback ladder on the live lookup (full URL, then sorted query params, then query-stripped URL, then path alone) and the shipped mechanism that consults the responder map and the regexp responder list stay in effect, so every request resolves to exactly the same responder as before the patch.
rubrics.rationale: Removal here is subtraction inside a live dispatcher; the coupling obligation is that nothing around the removed branch shifts - the case's behavior-preservation boundary lives at this file's core walk.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup stays internal: no exported declaration of package httpmock or internal is removed, renamed, re-typed or re-documented, and no new exported declaration is introduced by the patch.
rubrics.rationale: Some exported symbols (e.g. error helpers and the suggestion machinery near the respond area) are adjacent to edited regions; a tidy-up that exports, hides or renames public API would exceed the maintenance task this case asks for.

rubrics.criterion: The repair required no change to any test, example or build manifest file: no _test.go file, example, README or go.mod/go.sum entry is modified or added by the submitted patch.
rubrics.rationale: The case claims pure internal cleanup under an unchanged 171-case suite; a patch that touches the suite or the module manifest to make deletion convenient is not the behavior-preserving cleanup being graded, and deterministic runs alone cannot see such edits.

rubrics.criterion: No placeholder, tombstone or deferred variant of the parked rollout survives anywhere in the tree: no commented-out remnant of the strict engine, no re-introduced disabled switch or renamed gate, no registry kept 'for later use', no empty statistics collector, and no comment of the form 'reserved for strict mode' where the machinery used to be.
rubrics.rationale: Comment-out or stub-in-place passes compilation and lookups while keeping exactly the maintenance burden the task exists to remove; this is the canonical half-repair shape specific to a parked-feature cleanup and must not earn completion credit.

rubrics.criterion: No stale mention of the strict rollout survives in live code: identifiers, doc comments or comments inside surviving declarations still referring to the strict engine, its environment knob or its statistics (instead of being deleted along with the machinery they described) remain in the patch.
rubrics.rationale: The injected rollout carried narrative comments; keeping those comments in live code leaves documentation that misleads the next reader - a leftover specific to this instance that structural removal alone does not guarantee.

rubrics.criterion: The tolerant fallbacks were weakened or reordered: the live lookup no longer tries the full URL, then the URL with sorted query params, then the query-stripped URL, then the path alone in the shipped order, or the regexp responder consultation was altered while clearing out the parked engine.
rubrics.rationale: The likeliest overreach while deleting anything strict-looking is to cut a shipped fallback that looks like part of a two-engine story; those fallbacks are the shipped semantics, not remnants.

rubrics.criterion: Mock activation was altered: httpmock.Disabled no longer consults the same GONOMOCKS environment variable with the same meaning as before - for instance by renaming envVarName, wiring it to the removed knob's name, changing the emptiness comparison, or removing it as 'another leftover'.
rubrics.rationale: env.go is the smallest edited file and holds the real activation switch directly beside the removed knob; tidying the whole file is the plausible accident this instance invites.

rubrics.criterion: The parked canonicalization was 'finished' live: case-folding methods, stripping URL fragments, or otherwise changing how the shipped RouteKey maps registration keys (rather than deleting routeKeyV2, strictKey and canonicalRouteKey outright) so that registrations now match differently than in the shipped library.
rubrics.rationale: A solver who reads the intent of the v2 key may ship its canonicalization instead of deleting it; that converts dead scaffolding into new matching behavior - the exact opposite of the requested removal.
